Prevention: Rotate with non host crops e.g. legumes
Plant with first rains to avoid high incidence of the pest
Feed stalks to livestock or make compost with maize stalks or bury infested crop residues at least 30 cm deep by deep ploughing
Use trap crops such as sorghum or pearl millet or use the push-pull technology (plant desmodium between maize, and vetivar/napier grass outside) - factsheet available
Observe an area-wide closed season for at least 2 months
Place sand or soil in the funnel of the plant in hot spots, and in winter crop at the stage of forming internodes
Monitoring: Immediately after emergence, start monitoring and continue at weekly intervals until maize reaches physiological maturity
Check for holes on unfolding leaves, larvae and frass in and on the leaf sheaths
Check for dead heart (death of the growing point) among young maize plants
Consider control if you see one or two infested plants
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Apply 4 - 5 g of neem powder in the funnel of each plant.
The neem powder composes of neem seed powder mixed with dry clay or saw dust at a rate of 1:1.
Direct Control (Chemical): Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.

Observe a re-entry interval of 1 day and a pre-harvest period of 2 days.

Observe a 12-hour re- entry period and a 5-day pre-harvest period.
